title: PhonePe's Rahul Chari Charts AI Push for India's Next 300 Million Users
excerpt: The PhonePe co-founder says AI will increase feature velocity and enterprise value as the fintech moves to bring vernacular, privacy-first AI to 300 million first-time digital users.
body:
• PhonePe co-founder and CTO Rahul Chari says artificial intelligence will increase feature velocity and drive better enterprise value, laying out a charter for taking AI to the next 300 million Indians.
  • The fintech giant, with nearly 700 million registered users and 250 million monthly active customers, has automated 92% of customer support with AI.
  • Chari's strategy centers on on-premise open-source models for data privacy, AI guardrails against fraud, and natural-language interfaces in Indian languages to reach users who are not digitally native.
  • The goal, he says, is to make even basic digital payments universally accessible: "Don't optimize for the first million users. Optimize for the hundred millionth."

PhonePe's co-founder and CTO Rahul Chari has laid out his charter for deploying artificial intelligence at population scale — bringing AI-powered financial services to the next 300 million Indians, most of whom are not digitally native. Speaking in recent interviews with The Economic Times and Moneycontrol, Chari argued that AI will sharply increase the company's feature velocity and drive better enterprise value as PhonePe moves beyond its current user base.

PhonePe has evolved from peer-to-peer transfers to daily financial services, with nearly 700 million registered users and 250 million monthly active customers, according to Chari's conversation with YourStory's Tech Transformers series. The challenge now, he says, is onboarding feature-phone users and consumers who have never used digital services.

AI already doing the heavy lifting

Chari's case is built on what PhonePe has already automated. The company has automated 92% of customer support with AI, moved from rule-based systems to real-time AI decisioning, and uses unstructured data — voice, images, video — to generate sharper user insights. On the ET AI Podcast, Chari said the company automates more than 90% of support queries, runs on-premise open-source models to protect data privacy, and uses AI guardrails to fight fraud without sacrificing human explainability.

https://x.com/EconomicTimes/status/2097606734013731226

"This next set is still not digitally native, and it's going to take a fair amount of innovation to actually bring them on board," Chari told Entrepreneur India, pointing to AI's role in breaking down barriers of intimidation through vernacular interfaces and simplified user experiences.

"Don't optimize for the first million users. Optimize for the hundred millionth."

— Rahul Chari, Co-founder and CTO, PhonePe

Designing for "multiple Indias"

Chari rejects simplistic binaries between metro and rural users. "There are multiple Indias, and there are multiple Bharats," he said, arguing that even within metros, language personalization remains critical, while reaching less digitally mature segments requires deeper behavioral insight into how people build trust with financial tools.

He cited small product changes with outsized effects: a basic feature for transferring money between one's own bank accounts drove a 30% jump in transaction volumes, and simplified balance checks — which now exceed transactions — built user trust. "These are the kind of small things that make the platform significantly more sticky," he said.

Financial inclusion, in Chari's framing, is not just about offering products like insurance or lending but about ensuring even basic digital payments become universally accessible. On monetization, he is blunt: "We are an excellent user economy… but you need to focus on whether you're solving something that somebody is ready to pay for."

Privacy-first AI at the edge

Chari's technical blueprint centers on a privacy-first stack: on-device and on-premise models, natural-language interfaces that break language barriers, and AI on the edge for real-time decisioning. He argues that the shift from traditional software lifecycles to AI-driven systems means every business is effectively becoming a technology business — "the clear change that the pandemic has brought about," as he put it — and that the resulting wave of digital transformation will force organizations to rethink how they are designed from the top down.

"There are multiple Indias, and there are multiple Bharats."

— Rahul Chari, Co-founder and CTO, PhonePe

The diaspora angle

For NRIs, PhonePe's trajectory is familiar terrain: millions use the app to manage family finances back home, and India's digital public infrastructure — UPI, Aadhaar — is now the reference model for instant-payment systems being built across Asia, Africa and Latin America. Chari's bet is that the hardest remaining problem in fintech is not technology but trust and usability for first-time users — a lesson with obvious relevance wherever financial inclusion is incomplete, including within diaspora communities in the Gulf that transact heavily with India.

What's next

Chari's charter sets the bar for the decade ahead: moving from the first few hundred million Indians on the payments bandwagon to bringing the next 200–300 million onboard — building trust, designing simpler and safer products, and proving AI can expand access rather than just cut costs. With nearly half of India's population already on the platform, the next phase will be measured not in transactions alone but in how many people previously shut out of digital finance get pulled in.
nri_angle: NRIs managing family finances through PhonePe get a window into how AI will reach India's next wave of first-time digital users, a playbook the global fintech industry is watching.
author: Diaspora Desk
